form.label: 6. VMware / NSX — Microsegmentation Drift
form.description: Tie every "it stopped working on the other side again" back to the firewall rule or port-group change that actually caused it.

html.blockquote: "VMware, NSX im Einsatz, Mikrosegmentierung — ein kleiner Klick und es 'tut auf der anderen Seite wieder nichts', dann hat der Lieferant wieder ein Port gewechselt."
html.p: Microsegmentation is doing exactly what it's designed to do — blocking traffic that isn't explicitly allowed — but every time a vendor's application team changes a port, or someone edits a Distributed Firewall (DFW) rule or a port-group, something on the other side breaks with no obvious link back to the change that caused it. Without a log of who changed what, when lined up against the connectivity that broke right after, every incident starts as "is it the network or the app?" instead of "rule change at 14:02, app team, revert candidate".

panel.title: Data sources needed to build this for real

ul.li: NSX Manager — Distributed Firewall (DFW) rule create/modify/delete events, via syslog or the NSX API, including the rule name, source/destination, and the user who made the change.
vCenter events — port-group changes, VM NIC reconfiguration, and vMotion events (a VM moving to a different host/port-group is a common silent cause).
Change management / CMDB — a record of planned changes (ServiceNow change tickets), so an unplanned change stands out immediately.

Application-side connectivity checks — the kind of port/health probe this lab already runs for the web-app and DB tiers (port:probe, webapp:probe) — the "did it actually break" signal to correlate against.

panel.title: Time to root cause — before vs. with Splunk
Example: rule change immediately followed by an app outage

search.query: | makeresults count=4 | streamstats count as i | eval Time=strftime(relative_time(now(), "-".(240-i*20)."m"), "%H:%M") | eval Source=case(i=1,"NSX Manager (DFW)",i=2,"App probe",i=3,"NSX Manager (DFW)",i=4,"App probe") | eval Event=case( i=1,"Rule 'Allow-App-to-DB-5432' modified by user vendor.integrations (source range narrowed)", i=2,"webapp-berlin -> db-berlin:5432 probe FAILED (connection refused)", i=3,"Rule 'Allow-App-to-DB-5432' reverted by network.admin", i=4,"webapp-berlin -> db-berlin:5432 probe OK") | table Time Source Event | sort Time

panel.title: App connectivity around the rule change

search.query: | makeresults count=24 | streamstats count as i | eval Hour=strftime(relative_time(now(), "-".(24-i)."h"), "%H:00") | eval "App -> DB reachable"=if(i>=12 AND i<=13, 0, 1) | table Hour "App -> DB reachable"

panel.title: DFW / port-group changes by team (last 7 days, example)

search.query: | makeresults count=3 | streamstats count as i | eval Team=case(i=1,"vendor.integrations",i=2,"network.admin",i=3,"app.team") | eval "Changes"=case(i=1,7,i=2,2,i=3,3) | eval "Changes causing an outage <15min later"=case(i=1,4,i=2,0,i=3,1) | table Team "Changes" "Changes causing an outage <15min later"

panel.title: The SPL, once NSX + probes are onboarded

html.pre: index=nsx_dfw_events (action=create OR action=modify OR action=delete) | rename user as changed_by, rule_name as rule | append [ search index=*_web OR index=*_metrics sourcetype="port:probe" open=0 | eval rule="(probe failure)" ] | streamstats window=1 latest(_time) as last_change by rule | eval minutes_after_change=round((_time-last_change)/60,1) | where minutes_after_change>=0 AND minutes_after_change<=15 | table _time changed_by rule minutes_after_change
html.p: This is a smaller version of the Client → Hypervisor → App and Root Cause Analysis dashboards already in this lab, applied to "what changed" instead of "what's down".
